synopsis: The booklet treats Waymo as an on-road vendor precedent: its safety methods layer simulation, replay, closed-course and public-road tests, and shadow mode, using virtual methods as filters rather than substitutes for physical testing [f15718, f15729]. Waymo published collision-avoidance testing methods and documented city-by-city release in 2022, widening operating areas as evidence accumulates, but disclosed validation durations and physical-test shares do not establish verified sign-off [f604, f15720, f15728]. Its material distinguishes open-loop replay from closed-loop simulation; its dataset also illustrates the synchronized sensor data, calibration, poses and tracked labels needed for reproducible references, while its labeling study cautions that human labels can be inconsistent [f15721, f15722, f15723]. Waymo's world model announcement of 6 February 2026 remains an on-road vendor claim without off-road qualification; separate generative novel-view research reported 13.19–20.82 dB PSNR on Waymo data, which the booklet judges low fidelity for safety testing [f3759, f15724, f3821, f3822]. Waymo data also supported evaluation of December 2023 CARLA rain-lidar intensity prediction and the August 2026 Clear2Fog study using 270,000 images [f4739, f4897].
